domains.description: All rules governing table reservation creation, modification, cancellation, and invited-guest event management.

workflows.trigger: Customer submits booking form with date, name, email, and number of assistants
steps: 1. Validate booking date is in the future
2. Validate email format (text@text.xx)
3. Validate assistants >= 1
4. Check Terms and Conditions accepted
5. Query for free table with seats >= assistants in the booking time window (date - 1 hour to date)
6. If no free table: reject request with NoFreeTablesException
7. Generate booking token: 'CB_' + YYYYMMDD + '_' + MD5(email + timestamp)
8. Set expiration date = booking date - 1 hour
9. Set creation date = now
10. Set canceled = false
11. Assign table ID to booking
12. Persist booking record
13. Send confirmation email to host with booking token, date, cancellation link
business_rules: Booking date must be in the future
Email must be a valid email address
Number of assistants must be at least 1 (integer, max 2 digits)
Terms and Conditions must be accepted
A free table with enough seats must be available
Booking token format: CB_ + date + _ + MD5 hash of email+timestamp
Expiration date is booking date minus 1 hour
Cancellation link is valid until expiration date
exceptions: NoFreeTablesException: No available tables for the requested date and party size
InvalidBookingException: COMMON bookings cannot include invited guests

workflows.trigger: Host submits invitation form with date, email, and list of guest email addresses
steps: 1. Validate booking date is in the future
2. Validate host email format
3. Validate all guest email addresses
4. Generate host booking token: 'CB_' + date + '_' + MD5(hostEmail + timestamp)
5. Generate guest tokens for each guest: 'GB_' + date + '_' + MD5(guestEmail + timestamp)
6. Set expiration date = booking date - 1 hour
7. Persist booking and all invited guest records
8. Send confirmation email to host with token, guest list, and cancellation link
9. Send invitation email to each guest with accept and decline action links
business_rules: Host email must be valid (text@text.xx)
All guest emails must be valid
Guest tokens are prefixed with 'GB_'
Each invited guest gets an initial accepted=false status
Host receives confirmation with full guest list
Each guest receives individual invitation email with accept/decline links
Table is NOT assigned at invite creation; it is assigned 1 hour before the event based on accepted count

workflows.trigger: Guest clicks accept link in invitation email (contains GB_ token)
steps: 1. Validate guest token exists in the system
2. Set invited guest accepted = true
3. Persist updated guest record
4. Send acceptance confirmation to guest (with decline link for cancellation)
5. Notify host that guest has accepted
business_rules: Guest token must exist and be associated with a valid booking
Guest can change acceptance status multiple times before expiration
Host is notified of all guest acceptance/decline actions

workflows.trigger: Guest clicks decline link in invitation email or after prior acceptance
steps: 1. Validate guest token exists
2. Find and delete all guest orders (if any were placed)
3. Set accepted = false
4. Notify guest of decline confirmation
5. Notify host that guest has declined
business_rules: All orders placed by the declining guest are automatically deleted
Guest orders cannot remain after a guest declines

workflows.trigger: Host clicks cancellation link in confirmation email (contains CB_ token)
steps: 1. Validate booking token exists
2. Check current time < booking expiration date (= booking date - 1 hour)
3. If past expiration: throw CancelInviteNotAllowedException / InvalidCancelationTimeException
4. Find all invited guests for the booking
5. For each guest: delete guest orders, then delete guest record
6. Delete all booking orders
7. Delete booking record
8. Send cancellation email to host
9. Send cancellation email to each guest
business_rules: Cancellation must occur before the expiration date (booking date minus 1 hour)
Past the expiration date, cancellation is not allowed
Cancellation cascades: all invited guests and all orders are deleted
Host and all guests are notified of the cancellation

domains.description: All rules governing the creation, validation, pricing, and cancellation of food orders.

workflows.trigger: Customer submits order cart with booking token and selected dishes
steps: 1. Validate booking token is not empty
2. Determine order type from token prefix (CB_ = common, GB_ = guest)
3. For CB_ tokens: verify booking exists; verify no existing order for that booking
4. For GB_ tokens: verify invited guest exists; verify guest has accepted invitation; verify no existing order for that guest
5. Associate order with booking ID (and invited guest ID if applicable)
6. Persist order record
7. For each order line: set dish ID, amount, comment, extras
8. Persist all order lines
9. Calculate total price (sum of dish prices * quantity + extras prices)
10. Send order confirmation email with itemized cost and cancellation link
business_rules: Token must start with 'CB_' or 'GB_'; any other format is rejected (WrongTokenException/InvalidTokenException)
CB_ tokens require a valid existing booking
GB_ tokens require a valid existing invited guest
Invited guest must have accepted the invitation before placing an order (GuestNotAcceptedException)
Each booking can have exactly one order (OrderAlreadyExistException/OrderAlreadyDoneException)
Each invited guest can have exactly one order
Order line price = dish base price * amount + sum of selected extras prices
Order confirmation email is sent to the booking or guest email address
Email includes itemized dish costs, extras, and total price
Email includes a link to cancel the order
exceptions: NoBookingException / InvalidTokenException: Booking not found for CB_ token
NoInviteException / InvalidTokenException: Invited guest not found for GB_ token
GuestNotAcceptedException: Guest has not accepted invitation

workflows.trigger: Customer clicks cancel order link in confirmation email (contains order ID)
steps: 1. Find order by ID
2. Retrieve associated booking
3. Calculate cancellation deadline = booking date - hoursLimit hours
4. If current time > cancellation deadline: throw CancelNotAllowedException
5. Delete all order lines for the order
6. Delete order record
business_rules: Cancellation is only allowed before the configured hours limit before the booking date (mythaistar.hourslimitcancellation)
Past the cancellation deadline, orders cannot be cancelled (CancelNotAllowedException)
All order lines are deleted before the parent order is deleted

domains.description: Rules governing the dish catalog, categories, ingredients, and pricing.

workflows.trigger: Customer opens the menu page and applies category/price/likes/text filters
steps: 1. Compose filter request with selected categories, search text, max price, min likes, sort, and pagination
2. Translate frontend category names to server category IDs
3. POST to dish search endpoint
4. Retrieve matching dishes with images (Base64 encoded) and extras
5. Apply post-query category filter to include dishes matching any selected category
6. Return paginated results
business_rules: Category name-to-ID mapping: mainDishes=0, starters=1, desserts=2, noodle=3, rice=4, curry=5, vegan=6, vegetarian=7, favourites=8
A dish matching ANY of the selected categories is included (OR logic, not AND)
Duplicate dishes matching multiple selected categories are included only once
Dish images are returned as Base64-encoded strings
Sort is cleared if no sort property is specified
Default pagination applies if not provided (pageNumber=1, pageSize=5)

workflows.trigger: Customer clicks 'Add to Order' for a dish on the menu page
steps: 1. Create order item with unique UUID as local identifier
2. Set dish reference and any selected extras
3. Set default amount to 1 and empty comment
4. Dispatch AddOrder action to NgRx store
5. Update cart item count in header badge
6. Show order in sidenav cart
business_rules: Each cart item gets a UUID as a local identifier
Initial quantity is always 1
Multiple instances of the same dish can be added as separate line items
Price is calculated as (dish base price + selected extras prices) * quantity

domains.description: Rules governing user registration, authentication, roles, and two-factor authentication.

steps: 1. Validate username, password, and email
2. Check if username already exists in database
3. If exists: throw UserAlreadyExistsException
4. Encode password using BCrypt (PasswordEncoder)
5. Set default userRoleId = 0 if not provided
6. Persist user record
business_rules: Username must be unique across the system
Passwords are always stored BCrypt-encoded, never in plain text
Default role is assigned if no role is specified (roleId=0)
Registration requires username, password, and email

workflows.trigger: User submits login form with username and password
steps: 1. POST credentials to /login endpoint
2. Spring Security loads user by username via BaseUserDetailsService
3. Verify password matches encoded password
4. Resolve user's role to granted authorities
5. Return JWT token in response header
6. Store token and auth state in NgRx store
business_rules: Authentication fails if user does not exist or password does not match
User authorities are derived from RBAC role group tree
Undefined access control IDs are logged as warnings, not treated as errors
JWT token is issued on successful authentication
exceptions: UsernameNotFoundException: User not found or authentication error

workflows.trigger: Authenticated user enables 2FA from their profile settings
steps: 1. Toggle twoFactorStatus = true via user profile update
2. Request QR code generation for the user's account
3. If no TOTP secret exists: generate random Base32 secret and persist
4. Generate QR code URI from secret for authenticator app scanning
5. User scans QR code with TOTP app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.)
6. Subsequent logins require TOTP code in addition to password
business_rules: TOTP secret is randomly generated once and never regenerated
QR code is only generated if two-factor status is enabled
TOTP uses Base32 encoding for secret compatibility with authenticator apps

domains.description: Authorization rules defining what each role can access.

roles.description: Restaurant customers who browse the menu and place reservations/orders
capabilities: Cancel own orders within the cancellation window

roles.description: Restaurant staff managing daily orders and reservations
capabilities: View all reservations in the cockpit
View all orders in the cockpit
Search orders by email or booking token
Search bookings by date or email

roles.description: Restaurant managers with access to analytics features
capabilities: Access demand prediction cockpit (next-week dish forecast)

domains.description: ML-based demand forecasting and customer geo-clustering.

workflows.trigger: Manager accesses the prediction cockpit and submits forecast parameters
steps: 1. Manager provides start date, temperatures for each day, and holiday flags
2. Delete existing forecast data
3. Insert new forecast input data (temperature, holiday per day)
4. For each dish: check if ARIMA model training is needed
5. If not trained for this data range: prepare training data and run PAL_AUTOARIMA
6. Save trained ARIMA model parameters
7. For each dish: run PAL_ARIMA_FORECAST using trained model
8. Save prediction results
9. Return 7-day demand forecast per dish
business_rules: Model retraining is skipped if already trained for the given dish and start date (idempotency)
Training is skipped if no historical order data exists
Weather temperature and holiday status are covariates in the model
Predictions are generated for all dishes in the catalog
Only MANAGER role can access this feature

workflows.trigger: Manager selects a dish and date range for clustering analysis
steps: 1. Manager specifies dishId, start date, end date, and number of clusters (k)
2. Execute database clustering query with parameters
3. Return cluster assignments for all matching bookings
business_rules: Clustering is performed per dish within a specific date range
Number of clusters (k) is configurable per analysis
Only MANAGER role can access this feature

rules: Booking tokens for hosts are prefixed with 'CB_'
Guest tokens for invited guests are prefixed with 'GB_'
Token format: PREFIX + YYYYMMDD + '_' + MD5(email + YYYYMMDDHHmmss)
Tokens are used as authorization keys for booking and order operations
Token validity is tied to the booking expiration date
Booking expiration date = booking date - 1 hour
Booking cancellation allowed only before expiration date
Table search window = booking date - 1 hour to booking date
Order cancellation window = configurable hours before booking date (mythaistar.hourslimitcancellation)
Booking confirmation email sent to host on successful booking creation
Invitation email sent to each guest on booking creation
Guest acceptance confirmation email sent to guest after accepting
Host notified when any guest accepts or declines invitation
Cancellation emails sent to host and all guests when booking is cancelled
Order confirmation email sent to customer after order creation
Order email includes itemized dish costs, extras, and total price
All emails include relevant action links (cancel, accept, decline)
Dish line price = dish base price * quantity + sum of selected extras prices
Extras are deduplicated before price calculation
Total order price = sum of all line prices
Default page number is 1 if not provided
Default page size is 5 if not provided
All list endpoints support paginated responses
Deleting a booking cascades to delete all associated orders and order lines
Deleting an invited guest cascades to delete all guest orders
Declining an invite cascades to delete all guest orders
Order lines are deleted before their parent order is deleted
One order is allowed per booking (no duplicate orders per booking token)
One order is allowed per invited guest
